topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes for the hallmarks of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: It sets the framing, historical background, and learning objectives for the lecture on cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth signaling pathways and mutations driving proliferation and survival
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in cell surface receptor cascades, including Wnt and receptor tyrosine kinase pathways, lead to sustained proliferative signaling and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation block in hematopoiesis and carcinomas
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells stall normal lineage maturation and retain proliferative states in both blood cancers and epithelial tissues.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis via p53 and Bcl-2 family regulation
topics.groupedBecause: It details the biochemical mechanisms and key regulatory proteins cancer cells alter to prevent programmed cell death.

topics.label: Telomere maintenance, cellular senescence, and stress responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the mechanisms of replicative immortality, the cellular senescence barrier, and how stress pathways converge on p53 to govern cell fate.

topics.label: Cancer metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells rewire cellular metabolism, utilize aerobic glycolysis, and exploit metabolic enzyme mutations to drive tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis and neovascularization
topics.groupedBecause: It addresses how growing tumors overcome nutrient and oxygen limits by stimulating new blood vessel formation.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dissemination, and genomics of cancer metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the metastatic cascade from local invasion and circulation through to secondary site colonization and associated genomic features.

topics.label: Lecture summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: It provides closing framing and final summary remarks on the hallmarks of cancer.
